title: OI-Bench: An Option Injection Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Susceptibility to Directive Interference

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting an irrelevant multiple-choice option containing misleading instructions or structural disruptions (e.g., explicit commands, fake chain-of-thought, contradictions) and measuring the attack success rate (ASR) and accuracy drop.

Evaluating model susceptibility to authority and credibility cues by injecting options that cite government regulations, Wikipedia, academic sources, or expert endorsements to test if models abandon the correct answer.

Appending multiple-choice options that use gain-oriented cues (e.g., bonus points, money) or penalty-based coercion (e.g., zero scores, virus threats) to evaluate if models alter their decisions based on incentives or fear.

Permuting the position of the injected adversarial option from the default 'E' position to standard positions (A-D) to test if the model's vulnerability is influenced by the structural placement of the option.
